class_name: 意志-決定-コトニスル類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Marks a decision the speaker makes for themselves, with the inserted は setting that decision against a reservation, so が・ものの・けれど almost always follows (申し込むことにはしたが…). 〜ことになる is the counterpart for a decision handed down from outside, and 〜ようにする is about sustained effort rather than a one-off resolution. Takes the dictionary or ない form of the verb (行かないことにした).

examples.ruby: マラソン大会[たいかい]に申[もう]し込[こ]むことにはしたが、気[き]が進[すす]まない。
examples.english: I did go ahead and sign up for the marathon, but my heart isn't in it.

examples.ruby: 医者[いしゃ]に行[い]くことにはしましたが、まだ迷[まよ]っています。
examples.english: I've decided to see a doctor, though I'm still of two minds about it.

examples.ruby: 毎日[まいにち]記録[きろく]を付[つ]けることにはしたものの、三日[みっか]で終[お]わった。
examples.english: I made up my mind to keep a daily log, and it lasted all of three days.

glosses: make a point of …, for what it's worth
patterns.usage_note: Marks an ongoing effort to steer oneself toward a habit, with the inserted は setting it against a shortfall, so a concessive clause usually follows (返事をするようにはしているが…). Its classmate 〜ことにする reports a one-off decision already taken. ようにゃ is a colloquial squeeze of ようには and reads as rough or old-fashioned; ようには is the form to produce, with a negative on the verb (食べないようにする), not on する.

examples.ruby: 早[はや]く返事[へんじ]をするようにゃしてるんだが、つい遅[おく]れる。
examples.english: I do make a point of replying quickly, but I always end up late anyway.

examples.ruby: 毎朝[まいあさ]白湯[さゆ]を飲[の]むようにはしているが、効果[こうか]は分[わ]からない。
examples.english: I do make a point of drinking hot water every morning, though I can't tell it's doing anything.

examples.ruby: 玄関[げんかん]の靴[くつ]を並[なら]べるようにはしているが、夕方[ゆうがた]には崩[くず]れている。
examples.english: I do make a point of lining the shoes up in the entryway, but by evening it's a jumble again.
